answer: Graded discovery taper.** Each new agent identity publishes a beacon and must first transact within a narrow fee band; the band’s width shrinks as the count of recent new identities in that delta window rises. An attacker creating N identities faces a marginal cost that climbs faster than N, because each additional identity lands in a thinner band with fewer valid counterparties. A plume of affiliated identities also pays a discovery surcharge. Concrete cost: per-identity fees triple once the window exceeds its baseline, so mass registration compounds rather than scales linearly.
